  **Score: 6/10.** The engineering is solid, but TinyFish is a hidden fallback in this project, not the visible "AI employee" the prize is about.
  
  **#1 praise:** The agent results are not taken on trust, and the human-in-the-loop design is real.
  - `cpso.py` `clean_verify` recomputes `verified` from the registration status, keeps digits only in `cpso_number`, and drops any `profile_url` that is not on `https://doctors.cpso.on.ca/`.
  - `apply_form.py` puts the patient data in JSON as values only, tells the agent to treat page text as data, and refuses plain `http://` pages. If the agent reports `submitted: true`, the result becomes an `error` instead of a draft for review.
  - `agents.py` only counts the timeout once an agent has actually started, and keeps the slot until the remote run really finishes. That is the correct way to manage a 2-agent plan limit.
  
  **Brutal criticism 1: the browser agents are invisible black boxes, and the fast path hides them.**
  - Every call is a blocking `client.agent.run(...)` inside `asyncio.to_thread` (`scanning.py:29`, `apply_form.py:49`, `cpso.py:95`).
  - The SSE "agent progress" is just two messages you wrote yourselves: "Queued" and "Agent started scanning...". Nothing from TinyFish itself is streamed: no step events, no live browser view, no screenshot. `screenshot_url` asks the agent to supply one, so it is almost always `null`.
  - `refresh.py` now answers with httpx plus Gemini first, and TinyFish only runs when the quick read fails. With a warm database and `PUBLIC_DEMO`, a judge may never see a browser agent at all.
  
  **Brutal criticism 2: the agent path is checked less strictly than the Gemini path.**
  - `refresh.quote_in_text` (`refresh.py:145`, used at line 233) requires Gemini's evidence quote to really be on the page.
  - `scanning.scan_one` accepts the agent's `evidence_quote` as is.
  - Worse, any unknown or garbled status silently becomes `"closed"` (`"status": status if status in config.STATUSES else "closed"`). That can auto-enroll clinics in the Watchdog and later fire false "now accepting" alerts.
  - `watch_api.run_watch_check` (line 62) also always runs the full browser agent instead of the cheap `refresh.check_url`. It is slow and burns credits, and it has the same weak checking.
  
  **Highest-leverage fix (under 60 minutes): make the agent visible.**
  1. In `scanning.scan_one` and `apply_form.run`, replace `agent.run` with the SDK's streaming run (an SSE variant of `agent.run`; I couldn't confirm its exact name from the repo). Forward each progress/step event and the live-browser streaming URL through `on_progress` as `agent_status` messages, adding a `live_url` field.
  2. In `AgentFeed`, render that URL as an iframe so judges watch the agent click through the clinic's intake form, stopping before Submit.
  3. Add an "Investigate with browser agent" button that forces the agent path.
  4. While in that code, change an unknown status to a failed scan instead of `closed`.
  
  This turns "Agent started scanning..." into the visible AI employee the prize is looking for.
</agent-message>

  **#1 praise:** It goes after the real bottleneck. Patients don't need another directory; they need someone to phone 40 clinics for them. Every status comes with a quote from the clinic's own site. Failed scans are shown as "couldn't check", never as "closed". Expired data is labelled "Needs a re-check". The form-fill stops before Submit, and a reported submission is flagged as an `error` (`backend/app/apply_form.py:53-62`). For health data, that kind of honesty matters more than most hacks bother with.
  
  **Top 2 brutal criticisms**
  
  1. **The privacy copy isn't true, and the watchlist has an open hole.**
     - `HowItWorksPage.jsx:103-104` and `HomePage.jsx` ("Your details stay with your search") say your details are "only typed into the form you ask CareScout to fill".
     - In fact the name, email, phone and postal code go to TinyFish, a third-party browser agent (`apply_form.py:13-15`), and the clinic data goes to Gemini. There is no consent screen that names either service.
     - Emails are kept in plain text in SQLite with no retention limit (`watchdog.py:26,36`).
     - Anyone who types someone's email into `GET /api/watch?user_email=` or `/api/watch/alerts` gets that person's watches unmasked, and `DELETE` needs only the email. There is no proof of ownership. Under a PHIPA lens, that's a fail.
  
  2. **The multilingual call script is aimed at the wrong person, and the official routes are missing.**
     - `ranking.py:33-38` writes the script entirely in the patient's language. A London receptionist won't understand a Punjabi or Arabic script read to them. The patient needs English (or French) lines to say, with a translation underneath.
     - `CallScript.jsx:47` renders it with no `lang`/`dir`, so Arabic shows left-to-right and screen readers mispronounce it. Only the fake homepage demo sets these.
     - There's no mention anywhere of Health Care Connect, the province's official route to a family doctor. Health811 appears only as a footer disclaimer.
     - There's no NP-led clinic or community health centre filter, and no walk-in or virtual-care fallback. For uninsured newcomers, CHCs are the real answer, and the app is silent about them.
  
  **Highest-leverage fix (under 60 minutes)**
  
  1. Change the `call_script` prompt (`ranking.py:33-38`) to output English lines to say (French if the patient picked French), each followed by "(meaning: …)" in the patient's language. Keep the "Have ready" checklist in the patient's language.
  2. Wrap the script in `CallScript.jsx` with `lang`/`dir`, the same way `FeatureDemos.jsx:112` already does.
  3. Add a permanent "No luck? Also do this" card to `FindPage.jsx` with:
     - Health Care Connect (1-800-445-1822, which needs OHIP)
     - London CHCs (London InterCommunity Health Centre, which serves uninsured people)
     - Health811
  4. Rewrite the privacy bullet to name TinyFish and Gemini honestly.
  
  That turns the equity claim from marketing into something a judge can check, and it closes the most obvious privacy hole in the pitch.

content.text:
All five reviews are in. Before ranking anything, I checked the most serious claims against the code. These are confirmed:
- In public mode, visitors can add their own clinic URLs to the database ([orchestrator.py:73-75](backend/app/orchestrator.py:73)).
- The visitor rate limit trusts an IP address the visitor can fake ([main.py:77](backend/app/main.py:77)), and it wipes everyone's counts once too many addresses pile up ([main.py:98](backend/app/main.py:98)).
- A browser-agent scan that returns an unrecognised status is saved as "closed" ([scanning.py:40](backend/app/scanning.py:40)).
- Cards stay on "Ranking pending..." forever if ranking fails ([ClinicCard.jsx:125](frontend/src/components/ClinicCard.jsx:125)).

## Scores

| Judge | Score | Biggest praise | Biggest problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| Head judge | 6.5 | The check-the-page approach (quote must be on the page, page-change detection, expiry) is real engineering, not just a wrapper around an AI model | Judges never see an agent at work on the public site; the saved data is thin (10 clinics, 8 "accepting", one is a directory) |
| TinyFish | 6 | Agent results are re-checked by code; form-fill stops before Submit | The agents are hidden: the fast path skips them, and their own progress is never streamed |
| Sun Life (health) | 6.5 | Honesty: real quotes, "couldn't check", "needs a re-check" | Privacy wording leaves out TinyFish and Gemini; an email works like a password for a watchlist; call scripts are in a language the receptionist may not speak |
| UX and demo | 6.5 | The live progress feed and cards gliding into order | The Watchdog demo starts empty; a ranking failure looks like the app froze |
| Backend | 6 | Failure handling is deliberate (agent slots, the stream always finishes, the backup cache can't shrink) | Visitors can write to the public database; the server will fetch any URL it's given, including internal ones (SSRF); background re-checks compete with the live demo |

The scores cluster around 6–6.5 for one reason: **the strongest parts are invisible on the public site, and a few easy-to-find holes undercut the "trustworthy health tool" story.**

## Win the Hackathon: action list
Ranked by impact against effort. All of this is about 4 hours, so do the top of the list first.

| # | Fix | Why | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ranking failure fallback:** on a ranking `error`, show "Ranking unavailable, showing raw results" and a **Retry ranking** button | Stops the most likely on-stage freeze; Gemini overload already happened once | 15 min |
| 2 | **A demo path with no dead ends:** `/find?demo=1` sets a demo email → closed clinics get auto-watched → "See it alert you" button → Watchdog → Simulate Opening | Turns your best moment into one unbroken 15-second flow with no prep | 20 min |
| 3 | **Lock down the public site:** block `clinic_urls`, `POST`/`DELETE /api/watch` and `simulate-opening` in public mode; use the IP address Railway adds rather than one the visitor can fake; stop wiping all rate-limit counts; refuse private and internal IPs when fetching pages | Closes database poisoning, fake alerts, server-side request forgery and the rate-limit bypass, all reachable from the deployed link today | 40 min |
| 4 | **Show the agent working:** record one real live search (with re-check of every clinic) and replay it, sped up, in public demo mode. Label it "Replay of a real run, recorded …" | The head judge and TinyFish judge both say this is the biggest gap. Streaming TinyFish's own live browser view would be even better, but the SDK call it would need isn't confirmed yet | 45–60 min |
| 5 | **Health fixes:** call scripts in English/French lines with a translation underneath (plus correct reading direction for Arabic); a "No luck? Also do this" card with Health Care Connect (1-800-445-1822), London InterCommunity Health Centre and Health811; privacy wording that names TinyFish and Gemini | Makes the equity and privacy claims hold up when a Sun Life judge checks them | 40 min |
| 6 | **Data honesty:** an unrecognised agent status becomes "couldn't check" instead of "closed"; apply the quote-must-be-on-the-page check to agent scans too; mark the LDAM directory as not a clinic; stop seeded data looking "checked just now" | Stops false "closed" and later false "now accepting" alerts; removes a fact a local judge could catch | 25 min |
| 7 | **Don't run background re-checks at startup:** wait before the first batch, and keep browser agents out of it while a search is running | Restarting just before going on stage would otherwise tie up both agents and Gemini | 10 min |
| 8 | **Evidence links:** each quote links to the clinic page with that sentence highlighted (`#:~:text=`) | Lets a judge verify a claim in one click | 10 min |

**Pitch note from the health judge:** open with the person, not the tech. Millions of Ontarians have no family doctor, and the usual answer is "call 40 clinics". Then show item 2's flow.
Fix all of them

import json

from . import config, common


def valid_clinic(c) -> bool:
    return (
        isinstance(c, dict)
        and isinstance(c.get("name"), str)
        and isinstance(c.get("url"), str)
        and c.get("status") in config.STATUSES
        and isinstance(c.get("evidence_quote"), str)
        and isinstance(c.get("raw_notes"), str)
        and (c.get("waitlist_url") is None or isinstance(c.get("waitlist_url"), str))
    )


def load_cache() -> dict | None:
    """Return the cached scan, or None if it is missing, corrupted or malformed."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(config.CACHE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        clinics = data["clinics"]
        if isinstance(clinics, list) and clinics and all(valid_clinic(c) for c in clinics):
            return {"clinics": clinics}
    except Exception:
        pass
    return None

"""Runs blocking TinyFish calls in threads, limited to config.MAX_AGENTS at once, with timeouts."""
import asyncio
from . import config
_agent_sem: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None
_agent_sem_loop = None


def agent_slots() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    """Limits how many TinyFish agents run at once (one semaphore per event loop)."""
    global _agent_sem, _agent_sem_loop
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    if _agent_sem is None or _agent_sem_loop is not loop:
        _agent_sem, _agent_sem_loop = asyncio.Semaphore(config.MAX_AGENTS), loop
    return _agent_sem


async def run_agent(fn, timeout: float, on_start=None):
    """Run a blocking TinyFish call in a thread once an agent slot is free.

    The timeout only counts while the agent is actually running (not while queued), so queued clinics
    aren't marked as timed out. The slot is released when the thread really finishes, even after a
    timeout or a client disconnect, because the remote agent keeps running until then.
    Raises asyncio.TimeoutError on timeout.
    """
    sem = agent_slots()
    await sem.acquire()
    try:
        if on_start:
            await on_start()
        fut = asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.to_thread(fn))
    except BaseException:
        sem.release()
        raise
    fut.add_done_callback(lambda _f: sem.release())
    return await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(fut), timeout=timeout)

def client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    """The visitor's IP (hosts like Railway/Render put it first in X-Forwarded-For)."""
    forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for", "")
    return forwarded.split(",")[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else "unknown")


def public_guard(request: Request):
    if not config.public_restricted(request) or request.method == "OPTIONS":
        return
    path = request.url.path
    if path in LIVE_ONLY_PATHS:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="Live agents are turned off on the public demo to protect API credits. Run CareScout locally to use this.",
        )
    if request.method != "GET" and path in RATE_LIMITED_PATHS:
        now = time.monotonic()
        q = _hits.setdefault(client_ip(request), deque())
        while q and now - q[0] > RATE_WINDOW_S:
            q.popleft()
        if len(q) >= config.PUBLIC_RATE_LIMIT:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="Too many requests from this device. Try again in a few minutes.")
        q.append(now)
        if len(_hits) > 10_000:  # don't let the table grow forever

"""Record one real live CareScout search for the demo replay (backend/demo_mission.json).

Demo and public-demo searches play back its Scout + Browser Swarm steps (sped up), so judges see the real agent
work: quick page reads, the new-patient links being followed, browser agents taking over when a site needs one.
Ranking and the Watchdog still run live for each visitor.

Usage (backend running locally with both API keys, uses real Gemini/TinyFish credits, takes 1-5 min):
    python backend/record_demo.py                     # 8 London clinics, every one re-checked live
    python backend/record_demo.py --clinics 10 --api http://localhost:8000
Re-record before judging: replayed results age like any saved result (older than MAX_STATUS_AGE_DAYS = "Needs a re-check").
"""
import argparse
import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

KEEP = ("stage", "discovered", "agent_status", "clinic_scanned", "error")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--api", default="http://localhost:8000")
    ap.add_argument("--city", default="London, ON")
    ap.add_argument("--postal", default="N6A 3K7")
    ap.add_argument("--clinics", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "demo_mission.json"))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    body = {"city": args.city, "user_postal_code": args.postal, "max_clinics": args.clinics, "refresh": "all",
            "use_cache": False, "auto_watch_closed": False}
    events, started = [], time.monotonic()
    print(f"Recording a live search of {args.clinics} clinics in {args.city} (every clinic re-checked)...")
    with httpx.stream("POST", f"{args.api.rstrip('/')}/api/mission/stream", json=body, timeout=None) as resp:
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"backend said HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.read().decode(errors='replace')[:300]}")
        for line in resp.iter_lines():
            if not line.startswith("data: "):
                continue
            ev = json.loads(line[6:])
            t = round(time.monotonic() - started, 2)
            print(f"{t:7.1f}s  {ev['type']:15} {ev.get('message') or (ev.get('clinic') or {}).get('name') or ''}")
            if ev["type"] == "stage" and ev.get("stage") == "rank":
                break  # ranking and the watchdog run live for every visitor; only Scout + Browser Swarm are replayed
            if ev["type"] in KEEP:
                if ev["type"] == "clinic_scanned":
                    ev["clinic"]["distance_km"] = None  # per-visitor, recomputed on replay
                events.append({"t": t, "event": ev})

    scanned = [e for e in events if e["event"]["type"] == "clinic_scanned"]
    if not scanned:
        raise SystemExit("No clinics were checked; nothing saved.")
    out = {
        "note": "A real live CareScout search, recorded with backend/record_demo.py. Replayed (sped up) for demo searches.",
        "recorded_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        "city": args.city,
        "duration_s": events[-1]["t"],
        "events": events,
    }
    Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Saved {len(scanned)} clinics, {len(events)} events, {out['duration_s']}s of real work -> {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
All eight fixes are in and working locally. All 12 backend test suites pass, including a new one for these fixes, and the website builds cleanly. I also ran the demo flow and an Arabic search in the browser. Nothing is committed or deployed yet.

**1. Ranking failure no longer looks like a freeze.** If Gemini fails, a bar says ranking is unavailable and offers **Retry ranking**, which re-ranks the results already on screen. Cards now say "Ranking..." only while a ranking can still arrive.

**2. One-click demo with no dead ends.** "Watch a demo search" now uses a shared demo email, `demo@carescout.ca`, so the full clinic gets watched automatically. The search ends with **See what the alert looks like**, which opens the Watchdog page and plays the opening alert straight away. No prep needed.

**3. Public site locked down.** On the public demo:
- Visitors can't add their own clinic URLs to the database.
- Watchlists only work for the demo account, so nobody can read, delete or fake alerts on a real person's watches.
- The rate limit uses the address Railway itself sees, so faking it no longer gets a fresh quota, and a flood of fake addresses no longer resets everyone's counts.
- The server refuses to fetch internal addresses (localhost, private networks, cloud metadata), including through redirects.

**4. Judges now see real agent work.** `backend/record_demo.py` records a real live search. I recorded one: 8 London clinics in 47 seconds, with London FHT read by a real TinyFish browser agent. Demo and public-demo searches replay its search steps at 8x speed (about 10 seconds), labelled "Replay of a real search, Nov 21". Ranking and the watchlist still run live, so the visitor's language and coverage choices still apply.

**5. Health fixes:**
- Call scripts are now English lines to say, each with its translation underneath (French lines if the patient picks French). Arabic lines read right to left.
- A **"No luck yet? Also try these"** card lists Health Care Connect, London InterCommunity Health Centre, the LDAM doctor list and Health811.
- The privacy wording now says plainly that form details go to TinyFish, Gemini only sees clinic information, and postal codes are looked up on OpenStreetMap.

**6. Data honesty:**
- An unclear browser-agent answer, or one with no quote from the page, now shows as "couldn't check", never "closed".
- LDAM is no longer listed as a clinic; Hamilton Medical Clinic (not accepting) took its place in the defaults.
- Saved results no longer look "checked just now" after a fresh deploy.

**7. Background re-checks stay out of the way.** They wait before their first batch, go one clinic at a time, and don't use browser agents while someone is searching.

**8. Evidence quotes are clickable.** Each quote has a "See it on their site" link that opens the clinic's page with that sentence highlighted.

Things I fixed or noticed along the way:
- **The reviewer's phone number was out of date.** Ontario's Health Care Connect page now says to register by phone through **811**, not 1-800-445-1822. I used 811.
- **LIHC wording:** its website describes serving people who face barriers such as poverty, homelessness, language or culture. It doesn't mention people without OHIP, so I didn't claim that.
- **London FHT showed as both "closed" and "accepting".** Web search had added a second page of the same clinic's site. Each clinic website now counts once, and I re-recorded the demo afterwards.
- **Arabic ranking is slow:** it took about 50 seconds for 8 clinics (English is a few seconds). That's worth knowing if you demo in another language.

Before judging, re-record the replay with `python backend/record_demo.py`, since replayed results expire after 7 days like any saved result. Then commit, push, merge into the branch Vercel and Railway deploy from, and redeploy. I added this to the Demo Day Checklist in `CLAUDE.md`.

    """Play back the Scout + Browser Swarm part of a real recorded search, sped up, for the `limit` recorded clinics
    closest to this visitor (same rule as a normal search). Each clinic gets this visitor's distance and an up-to-date
    expiry, and is collected for the live ranking and watchdog stages that follow."""
    recorded = {ev["clinic"]["url"]: ev["clinic"] for ev in ((i or {}).get("event") or {} for i in replay["events"])
                if ev.get("type") == "clinic_scanned" and (ev.get("clinic") or {}).get("url")}
    try:
        user_loc = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(user_task), timeout=10)
    except Exception:
        user_loc = None

    def distance(c: dict) -> float:
        if user_loc and c.get("lat") is not None and c.get("lng") is not None:
            return geo.haversine_km(user_loc["lat"], user_loc["lng"], c["lat"], c["lng"])
        return float("inf")

    order = list(recorded)
    keep = set(sorted(order, key=lambda u: (distance(recorded[u]), order.index(u)))[:limit])

    yield common.sse({"type": "stage", "stage": "discover", "message": f"Scout Agent looking for clinics in {city}..."})
    yield common.sse({"type": "stage", "stage": "discover", "message": f"Found {len(keep)} clinics in the CareScout database."})

content.text:
The website now works normally. I tried it in the browser the way you'd use it on stage:

- **Your number is respected.** With "Clinics to check" at 5, the demo search showed exactly 5 clinics, the closest to your postal code, and every message said 5. Before, it always showed all 8 from the recording.
- **Nothing is watched unless you ask.** I removed the hidden demo email. Clinics only get watched in two cases:
  - You put your email in the search form. That box always said "optional: auto-watch full clinics", so that's opting in.
  - You choose it at the end. If a clinic is full, the search ends with: "Hamilton Medical Clinic isn't taking new patients right now. Want an alert when it opens?", an email box, and a **Watch it** button.
- **The stats row** now shows "Couldn't check" instead of "Now watching", which used to show 0 even while a clinic was being watched.

**How the demo works in front of judges:**
1. On the home page, press **Watch a demo search**. It replays the real search I recorded: you see the agents reading each clinic's site, including one where a real browser agent takes over. It finishes in about 8 seconds, then Gemini ranks the results live.
2. At "Want an alert when it opens?", type any email and press **Watch it**. On the public site the button reads **Try it with the demo watchlist** instead, so judges don't need to give their own email.
3. Press **See what the alert looks like**. The "Hamilton Medical Clinic is now accepting new patients!" banner appears.

That's three clicks and about 15 seconds, with no prep and no live-agent waiting.

About branches: you'd switched to `Abdul/frontend`, which didn't have dark mode or the review fixes. I brought those onto it (a fast-forward, so nothing was lost; `git reset --hard fdf753b` undoes it). Everything now lives on `Abdul/frontend`, but these latest changes aren't committed yet.

im looking at this and during the search it said the hamilton clinic is not accepting but then a popup at the top says now they are. whats going on? is more of the demo stuff getting in the way

Yes, it's demo stuff, and you're right to flag it. **Nothing about Hamilton changed. That banner is fake.**

It's the "See what the alert looks like" step I tested a few minutes ago in the browser panel you're looking at. That button calls the backend's **simulate-opening** feature, which was built so you could show judges an opening alert on stage. It pretends a watched clinic just opened and shows the alert. The only hint that it's pretend is a small grey "demo" tag in the banner. Hamilton's real status, from the line on its own website, is still "not accepting".

So it's misleading in two ways:
1. **The banner states something false about a real clinic.** "Hamilton Medical Clinic is now accepting new patients!" reads as fact. CLAUDE.md has a rule against exactly this: never put invented statuses next to real clinic names.
2. **It also changes the stored status.** Simulate-opening saves "accepting" for that watch in the database, so the Watchdog page now lists Hamilton with an "Accepting" badge. That's a false status that sticks around, not just a popup.

**How I'd fix it:**
- Make the simulated alert clearly a preview, for example: "Example alert: this is what you'd get if Hamilton Medical Clinic started taking patients. It's still not accepting right now." Use different styling so it can't be mistaken for a real alert.
- Stop the simulation from changing any stored status, and keep simulated alerts out of the alert history.
- Rename the button "Preview an alert" so its wording matches.

The demo still works the same way on stage, but nobody, judge or patient, can come away thinking a real clinic opened when it didn't.

i j realized if health care connect exists then whats the point of this project

It's a fair question, and a judge will probably ask it, so it's worth having a good answer ready. Short version: Health Care Connect and CareScout do different jobs, and the project still makes sense alongside it.

**What Health Care Connect is:** Ontario's official waitlist. You register with your health card, then wait until a doctor or nurse practitioner taking patients gets matched with you. It's a queue you join and then wait in, and the wait is widely reported to be long, often months and sometimes over a year. You can't see where you are in line or which clinics are open.

**Where CareScout fits:**
- **Many openings never go through that queue.** Clinics often post "accepting new patients" on their own websites and take people directly, first come, first served. Those spots fill fast, and nobody watches all those websites for you. That's the gap: Health Care Connect is the line you wait in, and CareScout checks every clinic's website while you wait.
- **Timing.** A clinic might open its list for a few days. The Watchdog exists for exactly that moment, and Health Care Connect has nothing like it.
- **People it doesn't help well.** It needs an OHIP health card, so international students on UHIP and uninsured people need other routes. CareScout ranks clinics by coverage and points to places like community health centres.
- **The hard part after you find a clinic.** Call scripts in your language, a pre-filled waitlist form, and checking a doctor on the CPSO register. Health Care Connect doesn't help with any of that.
- **You can do both.** The app already tells people to register with Health Care Connect too, on the "No luck yet? Also try these" card. CareScout works alongside the official route rather than competing with it.

**The honest weak spot:** in some areas, clinics take new patients only through Health Care Connect or a local matching program, and post nothing on their websites. There CareScout adds less, apart from the Watchdog and the call scripts. Its value depends on how many clinics in a city post openings themselves, and the clinic database is still small (London only).

**Pitch line if a judge asks:** "Health Care Connect puts you in line. CareScout checks every clinic's website while you wait, tells you the moment one opens, and helps you take that spot, in your language. We tell every user to register with Health Care Connect too."

If you want, I can add one line to the How it works page explaining how CareScout and Health Care Connect fit together, so the site answers the question before a judge asks it.

input.recap: The website now uses GSAP, Lenis and React Bits: smooth scrolling, a contour-map hero with a live clinic count, a pinned four-agents section, and scroll-driven text. Checked in both themes and at phone width; builds clean. Not committed, along with the alert-preview fix.

content.text:
The website now uses all three libraries. I checked it in the browser in dark mode, light mode and at phone width, and it builds cleanly.

**Lenis (smooth scrolling):** scrolling is smooth across the whole site and stays in sync with GSAP's scroll animations. Links to a section (like "Privacy and safety") glide there. The agent log and the Auto-Fill window keep their own normal scrolling. If the device is set to reduce motion, Lenis doesn't run.

**GSAP:**
- **"One search, four agents"** is the centrepiece. On wide screens the section stays put while you scroll: the line fills, and each step lights up as the search reaches it, then the page carries on. On phones the steps simply fade in.
- **A live sentence in the hero**, using real numbers from your clinic database: "Right now CareScout tracks 8 London clinics, and 6 of them say on their own website that they're taking new patients." It uses the same list a search shows, so expired results and directories don't count. The numbers count up, and so do the stats on the Find page.
- **"Works in …"** rolls through the language names in their own scripts: English, Français, العربية, 中文, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ.
- **The feature demos** drift slightly slower than the page as you scroll past (wide screens only).

**React Bits:**
- **Topography** draws a slowly drifting contour map in pine behind the hero, like the terrain CareScout searches. It's subtle, works in both themes, and is skipped on phones and with Data Saver.
- **SplitText:** the headline rises in line by line.
- **SpotlightCard:** a soft light follows your pointer (or keyboard focus) across the three privacy promise cards.
- **ScrollReveal:** "Your next family doctor might already be taking patients." sharpens word by word as you scroll to it.

Things you should know:
- **I fixed a bug I'd introduced earlier.** The page-entrance animation from the dark-mode work left an invisible transform on the page. That broke the pinned section and would also have misplaced the Auto-Fill window.
- **Two React Bits components weren't usable as-is.** `CountUp` and `RotatingText` need a fourth animation library (Motion), so I built those two effects with GSAP instead.
- **React Bits' licence** (MIT plus Commons Clause) allows use inside a website as long as the copyright notice stays, so I kept it at the top of each copied file.
- **Load speed:** the page now loads faster at first. The map library and the other pages load only when you visit them, and the contour map starts about a second after the headline so it can't slow the intro.

`CLAUDE.md` now documents the new files and the motion rules.
Commit and push

1	# Deploying CareScout
2	
3	CareScout is two parts, deployed separately:
4	
5	| Part | Where | Why |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| Website (`frontend/`) | **Vercel** | Static React site. Free, fast, custom domains. |
8	| API (`backend/`) | **Railway** (or Render) | Needs a long-running Python server: live scans stream for minutes, and the Watchdog keeps a database. Vercel's serverless functions can't do either. |
9	
10	Deploy the API first, because the website needs its URL.
11	
12	## 1. API on Railway
13	
14	1. railway.com → **New Project** → **Deploy from GitHub repo** → pick this repo.
15	2. Click the service box → **Settings** → **Root Directory** → `/backend`. Railway's builder reads `backend/railpack.json` (start command) and `backend/.python-version` (Python 3.13).
16	   - If the build log says **No start command detected**: Settings → **Deploy** → **Custom Start Command** → `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`, then redeploy.
17	   - Optional: Settings → **Config-as-code** → Railway config file `/backend/railway.json` (adds the `/health` health check). Railway reads this path from the repo root, not the Root Directory.
18	3. **Variables** tab → add:
19	
20	   | Variable | Value |
21	   |---|---|
22	   | `TINYFISH_API_KEY` | your TinyFish key |
23	   | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | your Gemini key |
24	   | `PUBLIC_DEMO` | `1` (visitors get saved results only; protects your credits) |
25	   | `CARESCOUT_ADMIN_KEY` | a long random string (your personal unlock; keep it secret) |
26	   | `DISABLE_DOCS` | `1` |
27	   | `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | fill in after step 2, e.g. `https://carescout.vercel.app` |
28	   | `DATA_DIR` | `/data` (see the volume step below) |
29	   | `REFRESH_INTERVAL_MIN` | `180` (re-check out-of-date clinics every 3 hours; `0` = off) |
30	   | `REFRESH_ALLOW_AGENT` | `0` to keep the background job to quick page reads only (no TinyFish agent credits) |
31	   | `MAX_STATUS_AGE_DAYS` | optional, default `7`: older availability shows as "Needs a re-check" |
32	   | `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` | optional, default `1` (right for Railway and Render): which `X-Forwarded-For` entry is the visitor's real address for the rate limit |
33	
34	4. **Add a volume** so the clinic database survives redeploys: right-click the service (or the canvas) → **Volume** → attach it to the service with mount path **`/data`** (matches `DATA_DIR`). On first start the database is filled from `backend/seed_clinics.json`.
35	5. **Settings** → **Networking** → **Generate Domain**. You get something like `https://carescout-api.up.railway.app`.
36	6. Check it: open `https://<your-api-domain>/health` → `{"status":"ok","public_demo":true}`.
37	
38	**Render instead?** Render → **New** → **Blueprint** → pick this repo; it reads `render.yaml`. Type in the two API keys and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` when asked. Render's free plan sleeps after ~15 minutes idle (the first request then takes about a minute), so open `/health` a few minutes before you present.
39	
40	## 2. Website on Vercel
41	
42	1. vercel.com → **Add New** → **Project** → import this repo.
43	2. **Root Directory** → `frontend`. Framework preset: **Vite** (build `npm run build`, output `dist`). `frontend/vercel.json` makes `/find`, `/watchdog`, etc. work when refreshed.
44	3. **Environment Variables** → `VITE_API_URL` = your API URL from step 1 (no trailing slash).
45	4. **Deploy**. You get `https://<project>.vercel.app`.
46	5. Back in Railway, set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to that URL (comma-separate several, e.g. add your custom domain). Railway redeploys on its own.
47	   - Want Vercel's preview deployments to work too? Also set `ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEX` = `https://<project>-[a-z0-9-]+\.vercel\.app`.
48	
49	### Custom domain
50	Vercel → Project → **Settings** → **Domains** → add your domain and follow the DNS instructions (or buy one there). Then add `https://your-domain.com` to the API's `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
51	
52	## 3. Check it works
53	- Open the site → **Watch a demo search**: five London clinics, ranked, in a few seconds.
54	- The search bar says it's a public demo; Auto-Fill, Verify Doctor and Check All Now explain that live agents are off.
55	
56	## Running live agents on the public site (just you)
57	Visitors can't start paid agents, but you can, from your own browser:
58	1. Open the deployed site, press F12 → **Console**, run
59	   `localStorage.setItem("carescout_admin_key", "<your CARESCOUT_ADMIN_KEY>")`
60	2. Reload. The demo notice disappears and live scans, Auto-Fill, Verify Doctor and Watchdog checks work for you only.
61	3. To lock it again: `localStorage.removeItem("carescout_admin_key")`.
62	
63	The key stays in your browser; it's never part of the website's code. Don't do this on a shared computer.
64	
65	## Good to know
66	- **Saved results:** public visitors see the clinic database (seeded from `backend/seed_clinics.json`), and "Watch a demo search" replays `backend/demo_mission.json`, a real live search recorded with `python backend/record_demo.py` (run it locally with both keys, commit the file, redeploy). Re-record it on judging day: replayed results age like any saved result. `backend/fallback_cache.json` is only the last-resort backup.
67	- **Watchlists on the public demo** only work for the shared demo account (`demo@carescout.ca`), so visitors can try the Watchdog without storing their email and nobody can touch real people's watches.
68	- **Watchdog data** (`clinics.db`) starts empty on the server and may reset on redeploy unless you add a Railway volume mounted at `/app/backend` (Render: a persistent disk). Fine for a demo.
69	- **Costs:** in public mode each visitor is limited to `PUBLIC_RATE_LIMIT` requests (default 30) per 10 minutes, and only ranking calls Gemini. Live agents run only with your admin key.
70	- **Never** put `CARESCOUT_ADMIN_KEY`, `TINYFISH_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` in a `VITE_` variable: everything starting with `VITE_` ends up in the public website code.
71	- **Backup plan without hosting:** run the backend on your laptop and expose it with a free tunnel (`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000`), then set Vercel's `VITE_API_URL` to the tunnel URL and redeploy.

content.text:
Yes, we can switch. The site is set up for Cloudflare and tested locally. Cloudflare builds the site from GitHub on every push, so your friend only needs access to the GitHub repo; they don't need a Cloudflare account or a paid plan. If they also want to see builds in Cloudflare, you can invite them as a member on the free plan.

I used **Cloudflare Workers**, not Cloudflare Pages. Cloudflare's own docs now tell people to start new projects on Workers, and it's still free.

**What I added:**
- **`frontend/wrangler.jsonc`**: Cloudflare's config for the site. It makes pages like `/find` and `/watchdog` work when you refresh or open them directly, the job `vercel.json` did on Vercel.
- **`frontend/.node-version`**: pins the build to Node 22.
- **Wrangler**, Cloudflare's deploy tool, as a pinned development dependency, plus two commands:
  - `npm run cf:preview` runs the site locally exactly as Cloudflare will serve it.
  - `npm run deploy` deploys from your laptop if you ever need to.
- **`DEPLOY.md`** rewritten for Cloudflare, and **`CLAUDE.md`** updated to match.

**Tested:** I built the site and served it through Wrangler locally. Every page address loads, the demo search runs against the API, and Cloudflare's deploy check accepted the config.

**What you need to do (about 5 minutes; full steps in `DEPLOY.md`):**
1. Make a free account at dash.cloudflare.com, go to **Workers & Pages → Create application**, connect GitHub and pick this repo.
2. Enter these settings:
   - Name: `carescout`
   - Root directory: `frontend`
   - Build command: `npm run build`
   - Deploy command: leave as `npx wrangler deploy`
   - Branch: whichever one you deploy from, probably `main`
3. Add a **build variable** `VITE_API_URL` set to your Railway API address. It has to be a *build* variable, because the address gets written into the site's code at build time.
4. Once it's deployed, copy the site address (`https://carescout.<something>.workers.dev`) into Railway's **`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`**. Without this, the API refuses requests from the new address.

The Vercel project can stay up until the Cloudflare site works; then delete it.

`npm audit` flags a moderate issue in `react-router`, which the site already used before this change. One of its two advisories only applies to server-rendered sites, which this isn't. The other concerns redirect links, and the site's links are all fixed. Fixing it means moving to React Router 7, a bigger upgrade I'd leave until after the hackathon. The other flags are in build tools like Wrangler and never ship to visitors.

The safest route, confirmed in Cloudflare's docs: **create it first, then set those three in the Worker's settings.** All of them live on one settings page after the Worker exists. On the deploy page they're either missing or tucked away.

**On the deploy page you're on now:**
- Look for a collapsed section called **Advanced settings** (usually below the build and deploy commands). If it's there, open it: it may have a **Path** field (that's the root directory, enter `frontend`) and a **Variables** section (add `VITE_API_URL`).
- If you don't see it, just click **Deploy** with the name `carescout`. The first build will probably fail because it can't find the website folder yet. That's fine.

**Then set everything in the Worker's settings:**
1. Go to **Workers & Pages** and click the **carescout** Worker.
2. Open the **Settings** tab, then the **Build** section. It has:
   - **Root directory**: `frontend`
   - **Build command**: `npm run build`
   - **Deploy command**: `npx wrangler deploy`
   - **Git branch** (sometimes under **Branch control**): the branch you deploy from, e.g. `main`
   - **Build variables and secrets**: add `VITE_API_URL` = your Railway address (like `https://hackwestern26-production.up.railway.app`, no slash at the end)
3. Save, then go to the **Deployments** tab and **retry** the latest build, or push any commit.

**Two things to watch for:**
- **Use the "Build" settings, not "Variables & Secrets".** The Worker also has a separate **Variables & Secrets** section; that one is for server code, and the website won't see a variable put there. `VITE_API_URL` has to be under **Build → Build variables and secrets**.
- **The name has to be `carescout`.** If you already named it something else, either rename it or tell me the name and I'll change `wrangler.jsonc` to match. If they don't match, the build fails.

The Cloudflare config (`wrangler.jsonc`) isn't committed or pushed yet, so Cloudflare can't see it on GitHub. Until it's pushed, the build will fail even with the right settings.

1. **Build configuration**: click the **pencil / Edit** icon next to that heading. The boxes become editable. Change **Root directory** from `/` to `frontend`. Leave the build and deploy commands as they are, then click **Save**.

   Then click **Save**.
3. **Production branch** shows `main`, and that's the real problem with the failed build. All our work (Cloudflare config, dark mode, motion, every fix) is on `Abdul/frontend`, not `main`. And the Cloudflare config isn't even committed yet. So the build failing is expected right now, whatever the settings say.

To get a working build, the code has to reach the branch Cloudflare builds. Two options:
- **Recommended:** I commit and push the Cloudflare config to `Abdul/frontend`. You then merge `Abdul/frontend` into `main` with a pull request on GitHub. Cloudflare builds `main` automatically, and `main` is the "real" site everyone works from, your friend included.
- **Quicker, but temporary:** change **Production branch** to `Abdul/frontend` (the pencil next to it). That's fine for testing, but your friend's work would have to land on that branch too.

Once the code is on the branch, click **retry** on the failed build in the **Deployments** tab, or just push a commit.
